questions.explanation: Compare how much is missing from a whole: 4/5 is 1/5 short, while 3/4 is 1/4 short and 7/10 is 3/10 short. The smaller the missing piece, the bigger the fraction.

questions.stem: Tom ate 1/4 of a bag of 36 lollies and his sister ate 1/3 of the bag. How many lollies were left?
questions.explanation: 1/4 of 36 is 9 and 1/3 of 36 is 12, so 21 were eaten and 36 − 21 = 15 were left. 21 is the number eaten.

questions.stem: Which of these lengths is the longest?
questions.explanation: Change them all to centimetres: 1.2 m = 120 cm, 1050 mm = 105 cm and 0.9 m = 90 cm. 120 cm beats 118 cm.

questions.stem: What is the smallest number greater than 30 that is a multiple of both 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: The common multiples of 4 and 6 are 12, 24, 36, 48 and so on. 36 is the first one above 30. 32 is a multiple of 4 only.

questions.stem: In a picture graph, each book symbol stands for 4 books. Liam's row shows 5 whole symbols and half a symbol. How many books did Liam read?
questions.explanation: 5 symbols are 5 × 4 = 20 books and half a symbol is 2 books, so 22. 24 counts the half symbol as a whole one.

questions.stem: How many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand turns all the way round, 360°, in 60 minutes. 20 minutes is one third of an hour, and one third of 360° is 120°. 240° is the turn in 40 minutes.

questions.stem: 50 students are going on an excursion in minibuses. Each minibus holds 12 students. What is the smallest number of minibuses needed?
questions.explanation: 4 minibuses carry 48 students, leaving 2 with no seat, so a fifth minibus is needed. 4 ignores the leftover students.

questions.stem: Three numbers in a row (like 4, 5, 6) add up to 48. What is the largest of the three?
questions.explanation: The middle number is 48 ÷ 3 = 16, so the numbers are 15, 16 and 17. 16 is the middle number, not the largest.

questions.stem: A bottle holds 2 L of water. How many 400 mL glasses can be filled from the full bottle?
questions.explanation: 2 L is 2000 mL, and 2000 ÷ 400 = 5. Check: 5 × 400 mL = 2000 mL. 50 comes from dividing 2000 by 40.

questions.stem: Pens cost 85c each. What is the greatest number of pens you can buy with \$5?
questions.explanation: 5 pens cost \$4.25, but 6 pens cost \$5.10, which is more than \$5. So 5 pens is the most.

questions.stem: A spinner has 8 equal parts: 4 blue, 3 red and 1 yellow. Which statement is true?
options: Yellow is as likely as red
Red is more likely than blue
Red is less likely than blue
questions.explanation: Blue has 4 parts and red has 3, so red is less likely. Yellow has 1 part, so it can happen but is the least likely.

questions.stem: A solid has 5 faces. Two faces are triangles and three faces are rectangles. What is the solid?
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end joined by three rectangles. A square pyramid also has 5 faces, but they are 1 square and 4 triangles.

questions.stem: 3 March is a Tuesday. What day of the week is 26 March?
questions.explanation: Adding whole weeks keeps the same day: 3, 10, 17 and 24 March are all Tuesdays. 26 March is two days after 24 March, so it is a Thursday.

questions.stem: A train leaves at 14:50 and arrives at 16:15. How long is the trip?
questions.explanation: From 14:50 to 15:00 is 10 minutes, 15:00 to 16:00 is 1 hour, and 16:00 to 16:15 is 15 minutes: 1 hour 25 minutes.

questions.stem: Sam thought of a number. He doubled it and then added 7. His answer was 31. What number did Sam think of?
questions.explanation: Undo each step in reverse: 31 − 7 = 24, then 24 ÷ 2 = 12. Check: 12 × 2 + 7 = 31.

questions.stem: I am a two-digit number. My digits add up to 13, and my tens digit is 3 more than my ones digit. What number am I?
questions.explanation: Pairs of digits that add to 13 are 9 and 4, 8 and 5, and 7 and 6. Only 8 and 5 are 3 apart, and the tens digit must be the bigger one, so the number is 85. 58 has the digits the wrong way round.

questions.stem: Matches are used to make squares in a row. 1 square uses 4 matches, 2 squares use 7 matches and 3 squares use 10 matches. How many matches are needed for 8 squares?
questions.explanation: The first square needs 4 matches and each new square adds 3, because it shares a side. 4 + 7 × 3 = 25. 32 counts 4 matches for every square.

questions.stem: 30 students were asked to choose one sport. Half chose soccer. One third of the rest chose netball, and everyone else chose cricket. How many chose cricket?
questions.explanation: Half of 30 is 15, so 15 chose soccer and 15 are left. One third of those 15 is 5 for netball, so 15 − 5 = 10 chose cricket.

questions.stem:
Ms Lee: Our class should grow vegetables in the school garden. Looking after plants every day teaches students to be patient and responsible.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Ms Lee's argument?
options: Students who cared for the class plants last year got better at finishing their jobs on time.
Tomatoes and beans grow best in a sunny spot that gets plenty of water.
Some students in the class say they do not like eating vegetables at all.
The school garden is next to the library and was built by parents last year.
questions.explanation: Ms Lee says caring for plants builds responsibility. Students getting better at finishing jobs after caring for plants backs this up. The other facts say nothing about patience or responsibility.

questions.stem:
Ana is older than Ben. Cara is older than Ana. Dev is younger than Ben.

Who is the oldest?
questions.explanation: From oldest to youngest the order is Cara, Ana, Ben, Dev. Cara is older than Ana, who is older than Ben and Dev.

questions.stem:
Ben: I should be allowed to get a puppy. I always remember to feed my goldfish, so I will remember to look after a dog.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens Ben's argument?
options: Ben has looked after his goldfish every single day for the last two years.
A puppy needs walking, training and feeding every day, which is much more work than a goldfish.
Puppies are among the most popular pets for families all over Australia.
Ben's neighbour has a cat called Smudge that often sleeps on their fence.
questions.explanation: Ben's argument depends on a goldfish being like a dog. If a puppy is far more work, feeding a fish does not show he can manage a dog. Two years of goldfish care would strengthen his case.

questions.stem:
In a code, each letter is changed to the next letter of the alphabet, so CAT becomes DBU.

What does DPEF stand for?
questions.explanation: To decode, move each letter back one: D to C, P to O, E to D and F to E, giving CODE. EQFG moves the letters forward instead.

questions.stem:
Zara: Every time I wear my blue socks, my netball team wins. So my blue socks make my team win.

Which statement shows the mistake Zara has made?
options: Zara's team may have won even more games last season than this one.
Zara does not say how many players there are in her netball team.
Blue might not be the colour of the uniform that Zara's team wears.
Two things happening together does not prove that one causes the other.
questions.explanation: Zara's team might win because the players are good, whatever socks she wears. Seeing two things together is not proof that one makes the other happen.

questions.stem:
At Kangaroo Creek School, students must wear a hat when they play outside in Terms 1 and 4. Everyone follows the rule. It is Term 4, and Priya is playing outside at Kangaroo Creek School.

Which one of these must be true?
options: Priya never wears a hat in Term 2.
questions.explanation: The rule covers Term 4 and everyone follows it, so Priya must have a hat on. The rule does not tell us about the weather, about Term 2 or about her hat.

questions.stem:
Ali, Bea and Cy each have one pet: a cat, a dog or a bird. No two have the same pet. Ali is allergic to fur. Bea's pet barks.

Who has the cat?
questions.explanation: Bea has the dog because it barks. Ali cannot have a furry pet, so Ali has the bird. That leaves the cat for Cy.

questions.stem:
Everyone in the chess club is in Year 4. Some people in the chess club also play soccer.

If these statements are true, which one of these must also be true?
options: Everyone in Year 4 is in the chess club.
Everyone who plays soccer is in Year 4.
questions.explanation: The chess players who play soccer are all in Year 4, so at least some Year 4 students play soccer. Nothing says every Year 4 student is in the club or tells us about other soccer players.

questions.stem:
School finishes at 3:10 pm and it takes Mia 20 minutes to get to her piano lesson. The lesson lasts 45 minutes and must finish by 5:00 pm.

What is the latest time the lesson can start?
questions.explanation: Count back 45 minutes from 5:00 pm to get 4:15 pm. Mia can arrive by 3:30 pm, so she is there in time. 3:30 pm is the earliest start, not the latest.

questions.stem:
Four friends meet, and each one shakes hands once with each of the others.

How many handshakes are there?
questions.explanation: The first friend shakes 3 hands, the second 2 new hands and the third 1 new hand: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. 12 counts every handshake twice.

questions.stem:
At the pool, you may only swim in the deep end if you have passed the swimming test. Everyone follows this rule.

Ali: Mei is swimming in the deep end, so she must have passed the swimming test.
Tran: Jo has passed the swimming test, so he must be swimming in the deep end.

If the information above is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Only people who passed may swim in the deep end, so Mei must have passed. But passing only allows Jo into the deep end; he could still be swimming in the shallow end.

questions.stem:
Five children sit in a row of five chairs. Ella sits in the middle. Finn sits at the left end. Gus sits next to Finn. Hiro does not sit at an end.

Where does Ivy sit?
questions.explanation: Finn is in chair 1, Gus in chair 2 and Ella in chair 3. Hiro is not at an end, so he takes chair 4, leaving chair 5, the right end, for Ivy.

questions.stem:
Mum: It is very cloudy this morning, so we should take umbrellas to the park.

Which of these has Mum assumed?
options: Clouds mean that it might rain.
The park is close to home.
Everyone in the family owns a raincoat.
questions.explanation: Mum moves from "cloudy" to "take umbrellas", which only makes sense if she thinks the clouds could bring rain. The other statements do not link the clouds to the umbrellas.

questions.stem:
Apples cost 40c each, or 3 for \$1.

What is the least it can cost to buy 7 apples?
questions.explanation: Two bags of 3 cost \$2 for 6 apples, and one more apple is 40c: \$2.40. One bag and 4 single apples would cost \$2.60.

questions.stem:
Coach: Our soccer team keeps losing because the players get tired in the second half. We need more fitness training.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens the coach's argument?
options: Our team's uniforms are new this year and are lighter than the old ones.
Fitness training would be held on Tuesday afternoons after school finishes.
Our team scores more goals than the other team in first halves but far fewer in second halves.
Some of our players also play basketball for a different club on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: If the team does well early and fades late, tiredness in the second half looks like the real problem, so fitness training makes sense. The other statements do not connect tiredness with losing.

questions.stem:
Sign outside a shop: Our ice cream is the best in town. Just look at our long queue!

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens the claim on the sign?
options: The shop sells twenty different flavours, including three that are dairy free.
Many customers who have tried it say the ice cream is the creamiest they know.
People in the town buy much more ice cream in summer than they do in winter.
The only other ice cream shop in town is closed this week, so everyone has to queue here.
questions.explanation: The sign uses the queue as proof of quality. If people queue only because the other shop is shut, the queue says nothing about taste. Customers praising the ice cream would strengthen the claim.

questions.stem:
2 apples weigh the same as 3 lemons. 1 lemon weighs the same as 2 strawberries.

How many strawberries weigh the same as 4 apples?
questions.explanation: 4 apples are double 2 apples, so they weigh the same as 6 lemons. Each lemon is 2 strawberries, so 6 lemons are 12 strawberries.

questions.stem:
A club meets every third day, starting on Monday 1 March, so its second meeting is on Thursday 4 March.

On what day of the week is its fifth meeting?
questions.explanation: The meetings are on 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13 March. 13 March is 12 days after Monday 1 March. 7 days later is Monday again, and 5 more days is Saturday.

questions.stem:
Oscar: Most children in my class like pizza. So most children in Australia like pizza.

Which statement shows the mistake Oscar has made?
options: Pizza first came from Italy, so it is not really an Australian food.
One class is too small a group to show what children all over the country think.
Oscar does not say which kind of pizza the children in his class like.
Lots of adults in Australia like pizza just as much as children do.
questions.explanation: Oscar uses about 25 children to decide about millions. His class might not be like other classes, so his conclusion goes much further than his evidence.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 5?
questions.explanation: The numbers are 14, 23, 32, 41 and 50. 05 is not a two-digit number.

questions.stem:
Principal: If we open a second serving window at the canteen, students will spend less time waiting in line.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens the principal's argument?
options: The canteen sells healthy food such as wraps, fruit cups and salads.
Some students bring their lunch from home and never buy from the canteen.
Students wait about 15 minutes now because one person has to serve every order.
The canteen opened ten years ago when the new hall was being built.
questions.explanation: If the wait is caused by having only one server, a second window would cut the wait. The other statements do not explain why the line is slow.

questions.stem:
In a race, Mo came 4th. Lee finished 2 places behind Mo. Kim finished 3 places ahead of Lee.

In what place did Kim finish?
questions.explanation: 2 places behind 4th is 6th, so Lee came 6th. 3 places ahead of 6th is 3rd.

questions.stem:
Dad: We should drive to the beach instead of catching the bus, because driving will get us there sooner.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens Dad's argument?
options: The bus costs the family less than paying for the petrol and the parking.
Dad enjoys driving along the coast road because the views are so lovely.
The beach has a kiosk near the car park that sells chips and cold drinks.
On weekends the beach car park is full, and finding a park can take more than half an hour.
questions.explanation: Dad's reason is speed. A long search for a park could make driving slower overall. The bus being cheaper is a different reason and does not show driving is slower.

questions.stem:
Train times between stations:

| From | To | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Amber | Beech | 12 min |
| Beech | Cedar | 9 min |
| Amber | Cedar | 25 min |
| Cedar | Dune | 8 min |
| Beech | Dune | 20 min |

What is the quickest trip from Amber to Dune, not counting waiting time?
questions.explanation: Amber to Beech to Cedar to Dune takes 12 + 9 + 8 = 29 minutes. Amber to Beech to Dune takes 32, and Amber to Cedar to Dune takes 33.

questions.stem:
One of three children left the gate open. Exactly two of them are telling the truth.

Amy: Ben left it open.
Ben: Cal left it open.
Cal: I didn't leave it open.

Who left the gate open?
questions.explanation: Test each child. If Amy did it, only Cal tells the truth. If Cal did it, only Ben tells the truth. If Ben did it, Amy and Cal both tell the truth and only Ben lies, which fits.

questions.stem:
In 4 years' time, Jade will be twice as old as she was 4 years ago.

How old is Jade now?
questions.explanation: Try 12: in 4 years she will be 16, and 4 years ago she was 8. 16 is twice 8. Try 10: 14 is not twice 6.

questions.stem:
Rule: If it rains on Saturday morning, the cricket match is cancelled.

The cricket match last Saturday was not cancelled. If the rule was followed, which one of these must be true?
options: It did not rain last Saturday morning.
It was sunny all day last Saturday.
Our team won the cricket match.
It will not rain next Saturday.
questions.explanation: If it had rained that morning, the match would have been cancelled. It was not cancelled, so it cannot have rained then. It could still have been cloudy, so "sunny all day" is not certain.

questions.stem:
Every child who helps clean up the playground gets a sticker.

Lucas: Ella got a sticker, so she must have helped clean up the playground.
Hana: Sami did not help clean up the playground, so he did not get a sticker.

If the information above is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: The rule says helping earns a sticker, but it does not say stickers are given only for cleaning up. Ella may have got her sticker another way, and Sami may have one for something else, so neither can be sure.

questions.stem:
A plant grows 3 cm on every sunny day and 1 cm on every cloudy day. Over 10 days it grew 22 cm. Every day was either sunny or cloudy.

How many days were sunny?
questions.explanation: If all 10 days were cloudy it would grow 10 cm. Each sunny day adds 2 cm more, and 22 − 10 = 12 extra centimetres means 6 sunny days. Check: 6 × 3 + 4 × 1 = 22.

questions.stem:
Every dog at the show has a ribbon. Some of the dogs at the show are poodles. Rex has no ribbon.

If these statements are true, which one of these must also be true?
options: Rex is not a dog at the show.
Rex did not want to enter the show.
questions.explanation: Every dog at the show has a ribbon, and Rex has none, so Rex cannot be one of the show dogs. He might still be a poodle that stayed at home.

questions.stem: Why did the knot in Hana's stomach loosen a little?
options: She already knew her first word.
She saw that the hall was nearly empty.
Kenji's waving made her want to laugh.
questions.explanation: Right after Kenji waves with both arms, Hana "almost laughed", and that is what eases her nerves. She does not hear her word until afterwards.

questions.stem: Grace's trick, "one collar, two sleeves", helps Hana remember
options: how many c's and s's are in the word
how to say the word out loud
which word she will be given next
questions.explanation: The story explains it: "One c and two s's, like a shirt." The trick is about spelling, not meaning.

questions.stem: "Hana clapped too, and found that she meant it." This shows that Hana was
questions.explanation: Meaning her clapping shows she was truly pleased for the boy from 4K, not just being polite.

questions.stem: Kenji shouts "as if she might not have noticed". This suggests that Kenji
options: thought Hana had not been listening to him
was confused about who had won the contest
was telling Hana something she already knew
had not watched any of the spelling contest
questions.explanation: Hana was on stage and knows she came second. The phrase gently pokes fun at Kenji's excitement in announcing it to her.

questions.stem: Which word best describes Grace?
questions.explanation: Grace practised with Hana all week, gave her a trick for "necessary" and already has one ready for "rhythm". That is helpful.

questions.stem: The poet calls the fig tree "a grandmother" mainly because the tree
options: is old and looks after others
is small and very easily hurt
is slowly losing all its leaves
questions.explanation: The tree keeps the little ones "safe", shades the cubby and feeds the animals, and it is "older than the houses", like a caring grandmother.

questions.stem: "She has enough for all" means that the tree
options: has room for every child to climb
has plenty of figs for every animal
is big enough to shade the street
has seen everything in the town
questions.explanation: The line follows the flying foxes coming to feed, so "enough" refers to the figs the tree provides.

questions.stem: In the last verse, what does the speaker plan to do?
options: Plant a new fig tree in the yard
Move a long way away from the street
Bring their own children to the tree
Cut down the old tree when it dies
questions.explanation: The speaker says "when I'm grown I'll bring my kids / to rest beneath her feet".

questions.stem: According to the article, what makes the echidna a monotreme?
options: It has a coat of sharp spines.
It is a mammal that lays eggs.
questions.explanation: The article says a monotreme "is a mammal that lays eggs". Spines, no teeth and where it lives are other facts about echidnas.

questions.stem: What does a threatened echidna do on hard ground?
options: Digs straight down into the dirt
Licks up ants with its tongue
questions.explanation: Digging down is what it does on soft ground. On hard ground it "curls into a prickly ball".

questions.stem: This article is mostly about
options: why an echidna is on the five-cent coin
how echidnas live, eat and protect themselves
how echidnas are different from platypuses
where to see echidnas in the wild
questions.explanation: Most paragraphs describe the echidna's body, food, defence and babies. The coin and the platypus are each mentioned only once.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits Gap 1?
options: The largest seed in the world comes from a palm tree and can weigh more than a bowling ball.
It is wrapped in a tough outer layer called a seed coat.
It soaks up the water and becomes plump.
Many seeds will not sprout if the soil is too cold.
It grows downwards into the soil, holding the plant in place and drinking up water.
questions.explanation: "This seed coat" in the next sentence needs a sentence that has just named the seed coat. The sentence about the largest seed fits none of the gaps.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits Gap 2?
options: The largest seed in the world comes from a palm tree and can weigh more than a bowling ball.
Many seeds will not sprout if the soil is too cold.
It grows downwards into the soil, holding the plant in place and drinking up water.
It soaks up the water and becomes plump.
Once it breaks through the soil, the first green leaves open.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says "As the seed swells", so the gap must explain how water makes the seed swell. The sentence about the largest seed fits none of the gaps.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits Gap 3?
options: Many seeds will not sprout if the soil is too cold.
The largest seed in the world comes from a palm tree and can weigh more than a bowling ball.
It grows downwards into the soil, holding the plant in place and drinking up water.
Once it breaks through the soil, the first green leaves open.
Some seeds are too old or damaged, and others are eaten by insects before they can sprout.
questions.explanation: "That is why gardeners plant in spring" needs a reason linked to warmth, such as seeds not sprouting in cold soil. The sentence about the largest seed fits none of the gaps.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits Gap 4?
options: The largest seed in the world comes from a palm tree and can weigh more than a bowling ball.
Once it breaks through the soil, the first green leaves open.
It grows downwards into the soil, holding the plant in place and drinking up water.
Some seeds are too old or damaged, and others are eaten by insects before they can sprout.
It is wrapped in a tough outer layer called a seed coat.
questions.explanation: The gap follows "the root" and comes before the shoot grows "the opposite way", so it should say the root grows downwards. The sentence about the largest seed fits none of the gaps.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits Gap 5?
options: The largest seed in the world comes from a palm tree and can weigh more than a bowling ball.
Some seeds are too old or damaged, and others are eaten by insects before they can sprout.
It is wrapped in a tough outer layer called a seed coat.
It soaks up the water and becomes plump.
Once it breaks through the soil, the first green leaves open.
questions.explanation: The shoot lives on stored food "until it reaches the surface", and "From then on, the leaves" needs the leaves to have opened. The sentence about the largest seed fits none of the gaps.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits Gap 6?
options: The largest seed in the world comes from a palm tree and can weigh more than a bowling ball.
Some seeds are too old or damaged, and others are eaten by insects before they can sprout.
It is wrapped in a tough outer layer called a seed coat.
It soaks up the water and becomes plump.
Many seeds will not sprout if the soil is too cold.
questions.explanation: "Not every seed grows" needs reasons, and planting two or three in each hole makes sense only if some seeds fail. The sentence about the largest seed fits none of the gaps.

questions.stem: Which extract describes something made from a cereal box?
questions.explanation: In Extract A the robot's body "was a cereal box".

questions.stem: Which extract tells the reader exactly how much of each thing to use?
questions.explanation: Extract B gives amounts such as "two cups of plain flour" and "half a cup of salt".

questions.stem: Which extract describes a smell bringing back a memory?
questions.explanation: When the writer of Extract C holds the wooden horse, they "can still smell that shed" from sixty years before.

questions.stem: Which extract gives facts about recycling?
questions.explanation: Extract D explains how plastic bottles are sorted, washed, chopped, melted and made into new things. Bolt the robot in Extract A is made from boxes, but that extract tells a story rather than giving facts.

questions.stem: Which extract describes a grown-up praising a child's work?
questions.explanation: In Extract A, Dad says the robot is "good enough to go in a museum".

questions.stem: Which extract includes a step that needs an adult's help?
questions.explanation: Extract B asks an adult to pour in the boiling water.

questions.stem: Which extract describes a gift?
questions.explanation: In Extract C, the writer's father made them a wooden horse, which they still keep. Bolt the robot in Extract A was made by the child for themselves.

questions.stem: Which extract says one way of doing something uses less energy?
questions.explanation: Extract D says recycling a bottle "uses less energy than making a new one from scratch".

questions.stem: Which text mentions wearing a helmet?
questions.explanation: Text A tells riders to wear a helmet, and in Text B Amira has leaves stuck in her helmet.

questions.stem: Which text gives instructions to the reader?
questions.explanation: Text A tells "you" to squeeze the brakes, press the tyres and check the chain. Text B tells a story.

questions.stem: Which text describes a fall?
questions.explanation: In Text B, Amira crashes into the hedge and scrapes her knee.

questions.stem: Which text mentions checking the brakes?
questions.explanation: Only Text A says to squeeze both brakes before a ride.

questions.stem: Which text shows a character who wants to keep trying?
questions.explanation: After crashing, Amira grins and says "Again".

questions.stem: Which text mentions a bike's tyres?
questions.explanation: Text A says to press on the tyres and pump them up if they are soft. Text B does not mention tyres.

questions.stem: Which text describes riding on a footpath?
questions.explanation: Amira wobbles "along the footpath" in Text B. Text A does not say where to ride.

questions.stem: Which text says how long it takes to learn to ride?
questions.explanation: Neither text gives a time. Text B shows Amira riding alone for the first time but not how long it took.
Count up from 2457: 3 makes 2460, 40 makes 2500, 3500 makes 6000 and 2 makes 6002. 3 + 40 + 3500 + 2 = 3545.

questions.stem: What is 4 × 125 × 7?
questions.explanation: Multiply in the easiest order: 4 × 125 = 500, and 500 × 7 = 3500. 875 leaves out the 4.

questions.stem:
Every student in a class named their pet. Students with no pet wrote "None".

| Pet | Students |
|---|---|
| Dog | 9 |
| Cat | 7 |
| Fish | 4 |
| Bird | 3 |
| None | 5 |

Each student named one answer. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation: Add every row, including None: 9 + 7 + 4 + 3 + 5 = 28. 23 leaves out the students with no pet.

questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 8 in 58 316?
questions.explanation: Reading from the right, the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The 8 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 8000.

questions.stem: What is 3/5 of 40?
questions.explanation: 1/5 of 40 is 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so 3/5 is 3 × 8 = 24. 8 is only one fifth.

questions.stem: How many metres are in 3 km 250 m?
In a picture graph, each star stands for 6 points. The Blue team has 3 and a half stars. How many points does the Blue team have?
questions.explanation: 3 stars are 18 points and half a star is 3 points, so 21. 24 counts the half star as a whole one.

questions.stem: What is 3.5 + 0.75?
questions.explanation: Line up the decimal points: 3.50 + 0.75 = 4.25. 3.80 adds the 7 and 5 in the wrong places.

questions.stem: A stack of cubes has 4 layers. Each layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes. How many cubes are in the stack?
questions.explanation: One layer has 3 × 5 = 15 cubes, and 4 layers have 4 × 15 = 60 cubes.

questions.stem: A bus leaves at 7:48 am and arrives at 9:15 am. How long is the trip?
questions.explanation: 7:48 to 8:00 is 12 minutes, 8:00 to 9:00 is 1 hour and 9:00 to 9:15 is 15 minutes: 1 hour 27 minutes.

questions.stem: A square has an area of 49 cm². What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: 7 × 7 = 49, so each side is 7 cm. Four sides of 7 cm make a perimeter of 28 cm.

questions.stem: What is the next number in this pattern? 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ...
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by one each time: +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6 and 16 + 6 = 22. 32 doubles 16, but the pattern is not doubling.

questions.stem: A normal dice numbered 1 to 6 is rolled once. Which of these is most likely?
questions.explanation: Greater than 2 means 3, 4, 5 or 6: 4 chances out of 6. An even number has 3 chances, less than 3 has 2, a 6 has 1 and a 7 cannot happen.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 3/4?
questions.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom of 3/4 by 3 to get 9/12. 6/10 would need a bottom of 8 to match.

questions.stem: Four concert tickets cost \$12.50 each. Dad pays with \$60. How much change does he get?
questions.explanation: Two tickets cost \$25, so four cost \$50. \$60 − \$50 = \$10. \$47.50 is the change for one ticket.

questions.stem: 4 apples have a total mass of 600 g. If the apples are all the same, what is the mass of 10 apples?
questions.explanation: One apple is 600 ÷ 4 = 150 g, so 10 apples are 1500 g, which is 1.5 kg. 6 kg is 10 lots of 600 g.

questions.stem: A farm packs eggs in cartons of 6. One morning there are 75 eggs. How many full cartons can be packed, and how many eggs are left over?
questions.explanation: 12 × 6 = 72, and 75 − 72 = 3 eggs left over. 13 cartons would need 78 eggs.

questions.stem:
The table shows the books Ruby read each month.

| Month | Books |
|---|---|
| January | 6 |
| February | 9 |
| March | 4 |
| April | 9 |
| May | 12 |

In which month did the number of books go up the most from the month before?
questions.explanation: February went up 3, April went up 5 (from 4 to 9) and May went up 3. March went down. May has the most books, but April had the biggest rise.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is both a square number and an even number?
questions.explanation: 36 = 6 × 6 and it is even. 25 and 49 are square numbers but odd, and 18 and 20 are even but not square numbers.

questions.stem: Jack faces east. He makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from east, a quarter turn faces south, a half turn faces west and a three-quarter turn faces north.

questions.stem: What digit goes in the box? $4\square \times 3 = 141$
questions.explanation: 141 ÷ 3 = 47, so the missing digit is 7. Check: 47 × 3 = 120 + 21 = 141.

questions.stem: Which shape has exactly 3 lines of symmetry?
options: A square, with all four sides equal
A rectangle that is not a square
A hexagon with six equal sides
A triangle with three equal sides
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle folds onto itself along the line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side: 3 lines. A square has 4, a rectangle 2 and a regular hexagon 6.

questions.stem: What is $20 - 4 \times 3 + 2$?
questions.explanation: Multiply first: 4 × 3 = 12. Then work left to right: 20 − 12 = 8, and 8 + 2 = 10. 50 comes from doing 20 − 4 first.

questions.stem: A tap drips 50 mL every minute. How long will it take to fill a 2 L bucket?
questions.explanation: 2 L is 2000 mL, and 2000 ÷ 50 = 40. So it takes 40 minutes.

questions.stem: Which number is exactly halfway between 36 and 84?
questions.explanation: The gap from 36 to 84 is 48, and half of 48 is 24. 36 + 24 = 60, and 84 − 24 = 60 too.

questions.stem: One light flashes every 4 seconds and another flashes every 6 seconds. They have just flashed together. How many seconds until they next flash together?
questions.explanation: The first light flashes at 4, 8, 12 seconds and the second at 6, 12 seconds. 12 is the first time on both lists. 24 works too, but it is not the next time.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers can be divided exactly by both 3 and 5?
questions.explanation: 75 ÷ 3 = 25 and 75 ÷ 5 = 15. 65 and 80 divide by 5 but not 3, and 63 divides by 3 but not 5.

questions.stem: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 7 cm apart on the map. How far apart are the real towns?
questions.explanation: Each centimetre is 5 km, so 7 cm is 7 × 5 = 35 km. 12 adds the numbers instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: A rectangular deck is 8 m long and 6 m wide. A corner piece 3 m long and 2 m wide is cut out for a tree. What is the area of the deck now?
questions.explanation: The full rectangle is 8 × 6 = 48 m², and the corner piece is 3 × 2 = 6 m². 48 − 6 = 42 m².

questions.stem: Ava is 3 times as old as her brother. Their ages add up to 32. How old is Ava?
questions.explanation: Think of the brother's age as 1 part, so Ava is 3 parts and together they are 4 parts. 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so the brother is 8 and Ava is 24.

questions.stem: In a class of 26 students, 15 have a dog and 9 have a cat. 4 of these students have both a dog and a cat. How many students have neither?
questions.explanation: Adding 15 and 9 counts the 4 students with both pets twice, so 15 + 9 − 4 = 20 have at least one. 26 − 20 = 6 have neither. 2 forgets the double count.

questions.stem: Today is Wednesday 28 May. May has 31 days. What will the day and date be 10 days from today?
questions.explanation: 28 May plus 3 days is 31 May, and 7 more days is 7 June. 10 days is 1 week and 3 days, so Wednesday moves on 3 days to Saturday.

questions.stem: Kim spent half of her money on a book. Then she spent \$6 on lunch and had \$9 left. How much money did Kim start with?
questions.explanation: Undo each step: before lunch she had \$9 + \$6 = \$15. That was half her money, so she started with \$30.

questions.stem: A spinner has 12 equal parts: 6 red, 4 blue and 2 green. About how many times would you expect it to land on green in 60 spins?
questions.explanation: Green is 2 parts out of 12, which is 1 in 6. One sixth of 60 is 10. 20 is the number expected for blue.

questions.stem: Two whole numbers multiply to make 36 and add up to 13. What is the difference between them?
questions.explanation: The factor pairs of 36 are 1 and 36, 2 and 18, 3 and 12, 4 and 9, and 6 and 6. Only 4 and 9 add to 13, and 9 − 4 = 5.

questions.stem:
Kai: Our class should have quiet reading time straight after lunch. It helps everyone calm down before maths.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Kai's argument?
options: Many students in the class say they enjoy reading comics more than novels.
Last term, the class made fewer mistakes in maths on days that started with quiet reading.
The school library bought 500 new books for students to borrow this year.
Some students find maths harder than any other subject they study at school.
questions.explanation: Fewer maths mistakes after quiet reading supports Kai's idea that it settles the class for maths. The other facts are about books or maths alone.

questions.stem:
Sam is older than Tia but younger than Uma. Vic is older than Uma.

Who is the second oldest?
questions.explanation: From oldest to youngest the order is Vic, Uma, Sam, Tia, so Uma is second oldest.

questions.stem:
Ruby: The new slide in our playground must be safe, because it is bright yellow and looks very strong.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens Ruby's argument?
options: The slide was put in during the school holidays by a team of builders.
Yellow is Ruby's favourite colour, so she was excited to see the slide.
Two children were hurt last month on the same kind of slide at another school.
Lots of children queue up to use the new slide every lunchtime.
questions.explanation: Injuries on the same kind of slide suggest it may not be safe, whatever it looks like. The other statements do not touch on safety.

questions.stem:
In a code, each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: A is 1, B is 2, C is 3 and so on.

Which word is written as 4 15 7?
questions.explanation: D is the 4th letter, O the 15th and G the 7th. COG would start with 3.

questions.stem:
Max: I didn't study for my last spelling test and I still got full marks. So studying is a waste of time.

Which statement shows the mistake Max has made?
options: He is deciding about all studying from just one test.
He does not say which words were in the test.
Spelling tests are only one small part of English.
His friend studied hard for the same test as well.
questions.explanation: One easy test does not show that studying never helps. The next test might use harder words.

questions.stem:
Every Saturday the Lim family either goes to the beach or visits Grandma. They never do both on the same day. Last Saturday they did not go to the beach.

Which one of these must be true?
options: They will go to the beach next Saturday.
questions.explanation: They always do one of the two things, and they did not go to the beach, so they must have visited Grandma. The reason they skipped the beach is not given.

questions.stem:
Grace: My friend said the new movie was boring, so I know I won't like it.

Which statement shows the mistake Grace has made?
options: She does not say how long the new movie goes for.
Her friend's opinion might not match what Grace would think.
The movie might be shown on television later on.
Her friend has seen lots of movies at the cinema.
questions.explanation: People enjoy different things, so one friend finding a movie boring does not prove Grace will. The other choices do not point to a problem with her reasoning.

questions.stem:
Oliver: Our class fish must be sick, because it isn't eating the food I just gave it.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens Oliver's argument?
options: Another student fed the fish a big meal ten minutes earlier.
The fish is bright orange with a long, white tail.
Fish need clean, fresh water to stay healthy.
The tank sits on a shelf near the classroom window.
questions.explanation: If the fish has just eaten, it may simply be full, so not eating does not show it is sick. The other facts give no reason for the fish to skip food.

questions.stem:
All the books on the top shelf are about animals. Some books about animals have photos in them.

If these statements are true, which one of these must also be true?
options: Some books on the top shelf have photos.
Every book about animals is on the top shelf.
Every book with photos is about animals.
A book about cars is not on the top shelf.
questions.explanation: Every top-shelf book is about animals, so a car book cannot be up there. The animal books with photos might all be on other shelves, so we cannot be sure the top shelf has any.

questions.stem:
A clock loses 5 minutes every hour. It is set to the right time at 9:00 am.

What time does the clock show when the real time is 1:00 pm?
questions.explanation: From 9:00 am to 1:00 pm is 4 hours, and the clock loses 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. A clock that loses falls behind, so it shows 12:40 pm. 1:20 pm adds the minutes instead.

questions.stem: In how many different orders can three children, Amy, Bo and Cy, stand in a line?
questions.explanation: Any of the 3 can be first, then either of the other 2 can be second, and the last one fills the end: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.

questions.stem:
At the zoo, only children under 5 get in free.

Nina: My brother got in free, so he must be under 5.
Ollie: My cousin is 7, so she did not get in free.

If the information above is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: "Only" means nobody else gets in free. So a child who got in free is under 5, and a 7-year-old cannot have got in free. Both are right.

questions.stem:
Four friends, Jo, Kit, Lu and Mo, sit around a square table, one on each side. Jo sits opposite Kit. Lu sits on Jo's left.

Who sits on Jo's right?
questions.explanation: Kit is opposite Jo and Lu is on Jo's left, so the only seat left, Jo's right, belongs to Mo.

questions.stem:
Teacher: Sophie got the top mark in the science test, so she must have studied the hardest.

Which of these has the teacher assumed?
options: Sophie enjoys science tests more than any other kind.
The student who studies the hardest always gets the top mark.
The science test was the hardest one of the year.
Sophie did her studying at the local library.
questions.explanation: The teacher goes from "top mark" to "studied hardest", which only works if the hardest worker always comes first. Sophie might simply know the topic well.

questions.stem:
Stickers cost 30c each, or \$1.20 for a pack of 5.

What is the least it can cost to buy exactly 12 stickers?
questions.explanation: Two packs give 10 stickers for \$2.40, and 2 single stickers cost 60c: \$3.00. One pack and 7 singles cost \$3.30, and three packs cost \$3.60 but give 15.

questions.stem:
Mr Daly: Cars drive too fast past our school, so we need a 40 km/h school zone sign.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Mr Daly's argument?
options: The school was built about 60 years ago, before most of the houses nearby.
Some parents walk their children to school instead of driving them there.
School zone signs are made of metal and have lights that flash at set times.
A speed check last month found that most cars passing the school were going faster than 40 km/h.
questions.explanation: Measured speeds above 40 km/h show that cars really are too fast, which supports the sign. The other facts do not show a speed problem.

questions.stem:
Leo is 6 years older than Mia. Two years ago, their ages added up to 14.

How old is Mia now?
questions.explanation: Two years ago each was 2 years younger, so their ages now add up to 14 + 4 = 18. Mia plus Mia plus 6 is 18, so Mia is 6 and Leo is 12. Check: two years ago they were 4 and 10, which add to 14.

questions.stem:
Advertisement: Zoom Shoes make you run faster. All the fastest runners at our club wear them.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens the advertisement's argument?
options: The fastest runners were already the fastest before they started wearing Zoom Shoes.
Zoom Shoes come in five bright colours and in sizes for both children and adults.
Zoom Shoes cost more than most other running shoes that are sold at the club.
Many people at the club now buy their running shoes online rather than in shops.
questions.explanation: If the runners were fast before the shoes, the shoes are not what made them fast. Price and colour do not tell us anything about speed.

questions.stem:
3 blue blocks weigh the same as 2 red blocks. A red block weighs 60 g.

How much does one blue block weigh?
questions.explanation: 2 red blocks weigh 120 g, so 3 blue blocks weigh 120 g and one weighs 40 g. 90 g mixes up which colour is heavier.

questions.stem:
Ferries leave the wharf every 35 minutes, starting at 9:20 am. Lucy gets to the wharf at 10:45 am.

When does the next ferry leave?
questions.explanation: The ferries leave at 9:20, 9:55, 10:30 and 11:05 am. Lucy just misses the 10:30 ferry, so the next is at 11:05 am.

questions.stem:
Ned, Olga and Pia each play one sport: tennis, swimming or netball. No two play the same sport. Ned does not swim and does not play netball. Olga's sport uses a ball.

What sport does Olga play?
questions.explanation: Ned plays neither swimming nor netball, so he plays tennis. Olga's sport uses a ball and tennis is taken, so she plays netball, and Pia swims.

questions.stem:
Sienna: Planting trees along our street would make it cooler on hot summer days.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Sienna's argument?
options: Trees are home to many kinds of birds, insects and possums in our suburb.
Some people in our street say they do not like raking up fallen leaves in autumn.
Our street was built about 30 years ago, when the suburb was first planned.
On hot days, streets with lots of trees were measured to be several degrees cooler than streets with none.
questions.explanation: A measured temperature difference supports Sienna's claim about heat. Birds and leaves have nothing to do with how cool the street is.

questions.stem:
Five runners finished a race. Ari finished before Ben but after Cat. Dan finished last. Eve finished just before Dan.

Who came first?
questions.explanation: Dan is 5th and Eve is 4th, so Cat, Ari and Ben take the first three places. Cat is before Ari, who is before Ben, so Cat came first.

questions.stem:
Library rule: You may have at most 5 books borrowed at one time.

Fatima has 4 books borrowed. She wants to borrow 3 more books today.

Which one of these is true?
options: She can borrow all 3 books now.
She must return at least 2 books first.
She must return all 4 books first.
She must return at least 3 books first.
questions.explanation: 4 + 3 = 7, which is 2 more than the limit of 5, so she must return at least 2 books. Returning all 4 would work but is not required.

questions.stem:
A ball is hidden under one of three cups. Exactly one of the labels is true.

Cup A: The ball is under this cup.
Cup B: The ball is under Cup A.
Cup C: The ball is not under Cup B.

Which cup is the ball under?
questions.explanation: Test each cup. Ball under Cup A: all three labels are true. Ball under Cup B: none of them is true. Ball under Cup C: only label C is true, which fits.

questions.stem:
Every student in the school band plays exactly one instrument. There are more drummers than guitarists, and more guitarists than violinists. There are 3 violinists.

Which one of these must be true?
options: There are fewer than 10 students in the band.
There are more violinists than drummers.
questions.explanation: With 3 violinists there must be at least 4 guitarists, and so at least 5 drummers. There could be more guitarists than 5, so "exactly 5" is not certain.

questions.stem:
Every Year 4 student at Hill School learns Japanese. Some students who learn Japanese also learn French.

Emma: Josh is at Hill School and learns Japanese, so he must be in Year 4.
Leo: Ivy is in Year 4 at Hill School, so she must learn Japanese.

If the information above is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Every Year 4 student learns Japanese, so Leo is right about Ivy. But other years may learn Japanese too, so Josh could be in another year, and Emma is wrong.

questions.stem:
A board is a 3 by 3 grid of small squares, like a noughts and crosses board.

How many squares of any size can be found on it?
questions.explanation: There are 9 small squares, 4 squares of 2 by 2, and 1 big 3 by 3 square: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.

questions.stem:
In a quiz you get 3 points for each right answer and lose 1 point for each wrong answer. Noah answered all 12 questions and scored 20 points.

How many questions did he get right?
questions.explanation: Check 8: 8 right gives 24 points, and 4 wrong takes away 4, leaving 20. 9 right would give 27 − 3 = 24.

questions.stem:
A snail is at the bottom of a wall 10 m high. Each day it climbs up 3 m, and each night it slides back 2 m.

On which day does it first reach the top?
questions.explanation: The snail gains 1 m each full day and night, so it starts Day 8 at 7 m. That day it climbs 3 m and reaches 10 m before it can slide back.

questions.stem: Why was Sam not pleased when Mr Martin asked him to show Ivy around?
options: He did not like having new students in the class.
He would have to miss his sport lesson that day.
He wanted to work on the Lego tower at lunch.
Mr Martin had been cross with him that morning.
questions.explanation: The story says he "had planned to spend lunchtime finishing the Lego tower". Nothing suggests he dislikes new students.

questions.stem: Sam "walked so fast that Ivy had to jog to keep up". This suggests that Sam
options: was running late for a lesson
wanted to show how fit he was
had lost his way in the school
wanted to finish the tour quickly
questions.explanation: Sam rushes through the canteen, oval and toilets in a few words, so he can get to the library and his tower.

questions.stem: The tower had begun to "lean like a tired tree". This means the tower was
questions.explanation: A tired tree droops and leans, and Raj fears it will fall. Ivy's fix makes it straighten.

questions.stem: How did Ivy know how to fix the tower?
options: Raj had told her exactly what she should do.
She had learned about wide bases from building at home.
She had read about towers in a library book.
Mr Martin had shown her how on the first day.
questions.explanation: Ivy explains, "We build stands for our water tanks at home," and that a wide bottom keeps the top up.

questions.stem: How do the boys' feelings towards Ivy change?
options: They go from liking her to being annoyed.
They stay cross with her the whole time.
They go from not caring about her to wanting her help.
They go from being scared of her to laughing at her.
questions.explanation: Sam rushes the tour at first, but after Ivy saves the tower he asks her to help finish it.

questions.stem: Which extract tells the reader what to do in an emergency?
questions.explanation: Extract A tells swimmers caught in a rip to stay calm, float and raise one arm.

questions.stem: Which extract describes boats at night?
questions.explanation: In Extract C the family watches the fishing boats come in during the evening, "their lights bobbing".

questions.stem: Which extract explains where sand comes from?
questions.explanation: Extract D says sand is made of rock and shell broken down by waves.

questions.stem: Which extract describes a plan being ruined by the sea?
questions.explanation: In Extract B a wave fills Mia's hole "in a single gulp" just before she finishes.

questions.stem: Which extract compares something to an insect?
questions.explanation: Extract C says the boats' lights were "bobbing like fireflies".

questions.stem: Which extract names a real place in Australia?
questions.explanation: Extract D names Shell Beach in Western Australia. The other extracts do not name any place.

questions.stem: Which extract describes a character laughing at a setback?
questions.explanation: Mia laughs after the wave fills the hole she worked so hard on.

questions.stem: Which extract explains what the flags on a beach mean?
questions.explanation: Extract A says the red and yellow flags show where lifesavers are watching.

questions.stem: What is $9 \times 8 - 4 \times 7$? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: Do both multiplications first: 9 × 8 = 72 and 4 × 7 = 28. Then 72 − 28 = 44.

questions.stem: What is a quarter past 2 in the afternoon in 24-hour time?
questions.explanation: Afternoon hours add 12, so 2 pm is 14:00. A quarter past is 15 minutes, giving 14:15. 02:15 is a quarter past 2 at night.

questions.stem: Nine students scored 4, 6, 6, 7, 9, 6, 4, 8, 5 in a spelling test. Which score happened most often?
questions.explanation: 6 appears three times and 4 appears twice; every other score appears once.

questions.stem: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has 3 edges around each triangular end and 3 joining the ends: 9. It has 5 faces and 6 corners.

questions.stem: How many 20c coins make \$7? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: 5 coins make \$1, so \$7 needs 7 × 5 = 35 coins.

questions.stem: I am between 40 and 50. I am odd, and I am a multiple of 3. What number am I?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 3 between 40 and 50 are 42, 45 and 48. Only 45 is odd.

questions.stem: A square has sides of 5 cm. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is the difference between their areas?
questions.explanation: The square is 5 × 5 = 25 cm² and the rectangle is 8 × 3 = 24 cm², a difference of 1 cm². 2 is the difference between their perimeters, 20 cm and 22 cm.

questions.stem: Ella ate 1/2 of a pizza and Max ate 1/4 of the same pizza. What fraction of the pizza is left?
questions.explanation: 1/2 is the same as 2/4, so they ate 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. That leaves 1/4. 3/4 is the part eaten.

questions.stem: The pattern starts 100, 93, 86, 79, ... What is the 8th number?
questions.explanation: Each number is 7 less than the one before. The 8th number is 7 steps after the 1st: 100 − 7 × 7 = 100 − 49 = 51. 44 takes one step too many.

questions.stem: A running track is 400 m around. Zoe runs 3 and a half laps. How far does she run?
questions.explanation: 3 laps are 1200 m and half a lap is 200 m, so 1400 m, which is 1.4 km. 1.2 km leaves out the half lap.

questions.stem: What is the smallest four-digit number that can be made using the digits 3, 0, 7 and 5 once each?
questions.explanation: A four-digit number cannot start with 0, so start with the next smallest digit, 3. Then place the rest from smallest to largest: 0, 5, 7.

questions.stem: A bag holds 20 marbles, all red or blue. The chance of picking red is 3 in 4. How many blue marbles are in the bag?
questions.explanation: 3 in 4 is red, so 1 in 4 is blue. A quarter of 20 is 5 blue marbles. 15 is the number of red marbles.

questions.stem:
Hamish: Students should walk to school, because the walk wakes them up and helps them concentrate in class.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Hamish's argument?
options: Some students live a long way from school and would need to leave home early.
Teachers noticed that students who walked to school were more alert in the first lesson.
Sneakers come in many colours, and most students already own a pair of them.
The school has a large car park for parents who drive their children to school.
questions.explanation: Walkers being more alert in class supports the link Hamish makes between walking and concentrating. The other facts are not about concentration.

questions.stem:
Four friends are in a queue. Pip is behind Quin. Rae is in front of Quin. Sol is last.

Who is first in the queue?
questions.explanation: Rae is in front of Quin, who is in front of Pip, and Sol is last. The order is Rae, Quin, Pip, Sol.

questions.stem:
Jess: Mum must be home, because her car is in the driveway.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens Jess's argument?
options: Mum's car is silver and was washed on the weekend.
Mum usually parks her car in the driveway at night.
Mum walked to work today and left the car at home.
The driveway was swept by Jess and Dad yesterday.
questions.explanation: If Mum walked to work, her car would be in the driveway even though she is out, so the car proves nothing. Mum usually parking there would only fit Jess's idea.

questions.stem:
No reptiles have fur. All snakes are reptiles.

If these statements are true, which one of these must also be true?
options: Some animals with fur are snakes.
Every animal without fur is a reptile.
questions.explanation: Snakes are reptiles, and no reptile has fur, so no snake can have fur. Not every reptile is a snake, and many animals without fur, like fish, are not reptiles.

questions.stem:
Toby: I saw three magpies swoop on people today, so all magpies swoop on people.

Which statement shows the mistake Toby has made?
options: Three magpies are not enough to show what all magpies do.
He does not say where he saw the magpies swooping.
Magpies are black and white birds found in Australia.
Swooping happens mostly in spring when magpies nest.
questions.explanation: Toby turns what a few birds did into a rule about every magpie. Many magpies never swoop, so his evidence is far too small.

questions.stem:
In a code, BIRD is written as DKTF.

How is FISH written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward 2 places: B to D, I to K, R to T, D to F. So F to H, I to K, S to U and H to J.

questions.stem:
Tim writes all the whole numbers from 1 to 20.

How many times does he write the digit 1?
questions.explanation: 1 has one, 10 has one, 11 has two and each of 12 to 19 has one. That is 1 + 1 + 2 + 8 = 12.

questions.stem:
Rule: If it is raining at lunchtime, students eat lunch in the hall.

Ana: Students are eating lunch in the hall, so it must be raining.
Bo: It is raining at lunchtime, so students must be eating lunch in the hall.

If the rule is always followed, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Rain means lunch in the hall, so Bo is right. But students might eat in the hall for another reason, such as a heatwave, so Ana cannot be sure it is raining.

questions.stem:
Nora reads 12 pages every 20 minutes.

How long will it take her to read 60 pages?
questions.explanation: 60 pages is 5 lots of 12 pages, so it takes 5 × 20 = 100 minutes, which is 1 hour 40 minutes.

questions.stem:
Mr Park: The new bike path will mean more children ride to school, so we should build more bike racks.

Which of these has Mr Park assumed?
options: Bike paths cost a lot of money for the council to build.
Children who ride to school will need somewhere to leave their bikes.
Some children would rather ride scooters than bikes.
The school has a sports oval beside the main car park.
questions.explanation: More riders only means more racks are needed if those riders need to park their bikes at school. The other statements are not part of his reasoning.

questions.stem:
Josh, Kara or Lin took the last mango. Exactly one of them is lying.

Josh: Kara took it.
Kara: Lin took it.
Lin: Kara is telling the truth.

Who took the mango?
questions.explanation: If Lin took it, only Josh is lying, which fits. If Kara took it, Kara and Lin are both lying, and if Josh took it, all three are lying.

questions.stem:
A pen and a pencil cost \$1.20 together. The pen costs \$1 more than the pencil.

How much does the pencil cost?
questions.explanation: If the pencil costs 10c, the pen costs \$1.10, and together they make \$1.20. A 20c pencil would make the total \$1.40.
